outcome_claim: Berkshire Hathaway had been buying KO since mid-1988 and disclosed in March 1989 a ~6-7% stake costing about $1.02B, later added to it, and never sold. Coca-Cola's earnings and global volume compounded strongly through the 1990s under Goizueta, and by 1998 the stock had risen roughly tenfold or more (after splits) to a very high P/E. It then stagnated for years after 1998, but it stayed one of Berkshire's permanent holdings.
